speaker: Unknown
en: And so I spend a lot of time trying to give back to the ecosystem.
zh: 所以我花很多时间尝试回馈这个生态。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I invest in a lot of young founders.
zh: 所以我投资了很多年轻创始人。

zh: 把直觉和你从业务的数字里看到的东西结合在一起。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think there's a sense of like, almost like working in real time with the world and having this real time conversation.
zh: 所以我觉得有一种近乎实时地与世界共同工作、进行这场实时对话的感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And based on that real time conversation, you inform your next move.

en: So what does that mean?

en: Yeah.

speaker: Unknown
en: And if it was so hard for me to ship an app, I couldn't even fathom an enterprise trying to figure out cloud computing and frameworks and tools and shipping pipelines and all of that.
zh: 如果发布一个应用对我来说都这么难，那我真的无法想象一家企业要怎么去搞懂云计算、框架、工具、发布流水线以及所有那些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I started a company with that simple premise, make it easy to ship.

speaker: Unknown
en: It took us about 10 years.

speaker: Unknown
en: Every time you ship a change to your app, that's a deployment.

speaker: Unknown
en: And then in the next 10 months, the 10 months since then, until now, we've added another 1.5 billion deployments.
zh: 然后在接下来的 10 个月里，从那之后的 10 个月直到现在，我们又增加了 15 亿次部署。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what took us 10 years, we've now surpassed in just a few months.
zh: 所以我们花了 10 年才做到的事，现在只用几个月就超越了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason for this is that...
zh: 而原因是……

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, one, shipping has gotten easier.

speaker: Unknown
en: Not gotten easier in the sense that like the code is actually pretty dumb hard, but now we have coding agents writing the code.

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think nobody ever saw that coming.

speaker: Unknown
en: The people building the AI, the people close to the AI, I think what's been the supersonic tsunami is that the machines have taken over, they're better than us at figuring out these algorithms, this code, but they need to ship that stuff somewhere.

speaker: Unknown
en: Like when you write the code, you know, code is kind of a funny thing.

en: Like I remember telling people another one of my sort of internal principles is code is a liability.

speaker: Unknown
en: Code can have vulnerabilities.

speaker: Unknown
en: Code is how, you know, you could delete stuff.
zh: 代码就是那种，你知道，你可以删掉东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can, you know, leak customer data.
zh: 你可以，你知道，泄露客户数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: So like code is like you have to treat code with responsibility.

speaker: Unknown
en: But now, you know, these coding agents are superhuman at writing the most amazing code.

en: But again, code doesn't do anything by its own.

speaker: Unknown
en: It needs to live somewhere.

speaker: Unknown
en: It needs to be deployed.

en: And Vercel has sort of emerged as the place, this universal field where all of the coding agents are plugging into and pushing their code out so that it can be used by anybody.
zh: 而 Vercel 已经成为那个地方，这个通用的场域，所有的编程智能体都接入进来并推送它们的代码，让任何人都能使用。

zh: 所以你可能每天都在使用 Vercel，因为当你在 X 上看到东西爆火时，现在这让我相当自豪，对吧？
